cleanIntro: The Super X4 is a gas autoloader whose Active Valve piston system rides on the magazine tube, so the strip is unusual: taking the forearm off is what exposes the gas parts, and they simply slide forward off the tube with the barrel. Winchester sets three levels of cleaning — wipe down with the barrel on, barrel and gas system off for a proper clean, and bolt and trigger group out for a complete one — and states that the bolt and trigger group are designed to come out in the field with no special tools. That is where the published strip stops: beyond the bolt assembly and the trigger group is a gunsmith's job, and both parts carry their own do-not-go-further notice. Two things fork by model. The 12 and 20 gauge guns differ in how the bolt handle comes out, and every step below is governed by one rule — the action must never be let slam shut with the barrel off.

steps.title: Cycle it dry until the bolt locks back, then look
steps.action: Safety on safe, then work the bolt handle repeatedly, catching each shell as it is lifted from the magazine, chambered and ejected. When the tube is empty the bolt locks rearward on its own — that lock-back is information, not a conclusion. Look into the chamber, at the carrier and feed mechanism and up into the magazine before you accept it. On a gas gun a shell can also be sitting on the carrier where the open bolt hides it.
steps.prose: Try not to let ejected shells hit the ground; a dented hull is a feeding problem waiting for the next outing.
steps.quote: EVEN WITH THE BOLT LOCKED OPEN AFTER SHOOTING, DO NOT ASSUME THE SHOTGUN IS UNLOADED. ALWAYS INSPECT THE CHAMBER, FEED MECHANISM, AND MAGAZINE TO BE CERTAIN THE SHOTGUN IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Firing
steps.warn: A locked-back bolt is not a clearance. Look at chamber, feed mechanism and magazine.

steps.title: Your safety may be set for the other hand — check before you trust it
steps.action: Find the crossbolt safety at the REAR of the trigger guard and verify which way is safe on your gun. Every Super X4 safety is reversible, and Winchester ships right-hand guns with it in the right-hand position and left-hand guns in the left-hand position — so on a right-hand gun, safe is pushed to the RIGHT and the red band shows when it is off. On a left-hand gun that is exactly reversed. A shotgun bought used may have been reversed by a previous owner, and the button gives no external clue which way it is set.
steps.prose: Reversing it is not an owner operation: Winchester routes that to an authorised repair centre or the Arnold service facility.
steps.caution: Verify which direction is safe on YOUR gun before handling it.
steps.quote: The “safety” on both right-hand versions and left-hand versions of the Super X®4 is reversible for right- or left-handed operation.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operation of the "Safety"

steps.title: Never let the action slam shut with the barrel off
steps.action: Learn this before the barrel comes off, because it applies at four separate points in the strip and reassembly. With the barrel removed there is nothing to arrest the bolt's forward travel in the normal way, and pressing the bolt release lets the bolt run home hard enough to drive the bolt handle into the receiver. The damage is to the receiver and the handle, and it is instant. When the bolt must be moved forward with the barrel off, HOLD the bolt handle and ease it forward while pressing the release — never press the release alone.
steps.prose: Winchester also says to leave the bolt rearward once the barrel is off, which is the simplest way to avoid the whole problem.
steps.quote: NOTICE: NEVER ALLOW THE ACTION TO SLAM CLOSED BY PRESSING THE BOLT RELEASE BUTTON WITHOUT THE BARREL INSTALLED. IF THE BOLT IS RELEASED FORWARD WITH THE BARREL REMOVED, THE BOLT HANDLE WILL HIT THE RECEIVER AND CAUSE DAMAGE.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REMOVING THE TRIGGER GROUP, step 1 NOTICE
steps.warn: Barrel off = never press the bolt release without holding the handle.

steps.title: Magazine cap off, forearm forward off the magazine tube
steps.action: Lock the bolt to the rear first, then unscrew the magazine cap and slide the forearm forward off the magazine tube. On the SX4 the forearm is not just a handhold — it covers the gas bracket and the piston parts, so this is the step that opens up the gas system. If yours is a wood forearm, take it by the sides rather than gripping the open rear end: squeezing that end is how a wood forearm splits, and the manual warns about it specifically.
steps.prose: Composite forearms are not fragile in the same way, but the habit is worth keeping.
steps.caution: Wood forearm: never squeeze the open rear end.
steps.quote: NOTICE: DO NOT SQUEEZE HARD ON THE OPEN REAR END OF A WOOD FOREARM. TOO MUCH PRESSURE COULD CAUSE THE WOOD TO SPLIT.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Assembly, step 2 NOTICE

steps.title: Barrel and the three gas parts slide forward together off the tube
steps.action: Draw the barrel, the gas piston, the piston sleeve and the piston sleeve spring FORWARD off the magazine tube as a group. The whole Active Valve system rides on that tube — piston in the gas bracket, sleeve and spring behind it — so there is nothing to unscrew and nothing to prise; it comes off in the direction the muzzle points. Keep those three gas parts together and note their order as they leave the tube, because the sleeve goes back on push-rod end first and the push rod has a side.
steps.prose: If you are only stripping for storage, put the spring, sleeve and piston back on the tube, refit the forearm and cap, and you have two compact units: the barrel, and the action with stock and forearm.
steps.quote: For cleaning, remove the barrel, gas piston, piston sleeve, and piston sleeve spring by sliding them forward off the magazine tube.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly, step 3

steps.title: Chamber length is not negotiable in either direction
steps.action: If you are swapping barrels, read the chamber length inscribed on the side of the barrel and match it to the gun. Winchester bars a 3½ inch barrel on a shotgun built for 3 inch barrels and equally bars a 3 inch barrel on a 3½ inch gun — the bar runs both ways, because the two guns differ in more than the chamber. A barrel that threads on and locks up is not evidence of compatibility; the receiver, the carrier and the gas system are all sized to the gun's own shell length.
steps.prose: Chamber length also decides which shells the gun can eat, and a 3 inch SX4 is explicitly not designed for the lightest 7/8 and 1 ounce target loads.
steps.quote: Never use a barrel with a 3½" chamber on a shotgun designed for barrels with a 3" chamber.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Extra Barrels
steps.warn: 3½ inch barrel on a 3 inch gun — and the reverse — are both forbidden.

steps.title: An SX1, SX2 or SX3 barrel is NOT an SX4 barrel
steps.action: The other half of the barrel rule catches the trap nobody expects: earlier Super X shotguns from the same maker. Winchester names the Super X1, Super X2 and Super X3 and bars all of them, along with any other manufacturer's barrel. These are the barrels most likely to turn up in the same gun cabinet or on the same used rack, they carry similar markings, and some will physically go on. The gas system, the barrel extension and the lockup are what differ, and none of that is visible with the barrel in your hands.
steps.prose: Within a gauge and chamber length, genuine SX4 barrels interchange with no fitting at all. That is what makes the wrong barrel so easy to believe in.
steps.quote: Never use a barrel from other Winchester shotguns, including those for the Super X®1, Super X®2, or Super X®3.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Extra Barrels
steps.warn: No SX1, SX2 or SX3 barrel on an SX4. No other maker's barrel either.

steps.title: Two assemblies come out, and that is the published boundary
steps.action: Before you take the action apart, know where it stops. Winchester defines action disassembly as exactly two things — the bolt assembly and the trigger group — and puts anything beyond that with a qualified gunsmith. Both come out in the field without special tools, which is a design feature of this shotgun rather than a concession. Work in that order too: trigger group first, then bolt, because the bolt removal procedure begins by telling you the trigger group is already out.
steps.prose: The reason to go this far is a specific one — an action that has got excessively dirty or wet. It is not a per-outing job.
steps.caution: Bolt assembly and trigger group. Nothing beyond.
steps.quote: Disassembly of the action involves the removal of the bolt assembly and the trigger group. Disassembly beyond this point should only be performed by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies

steps.title: Trigger group pins out, then lift the trigger guard up and out
steps.action: Hold the bolt handle and ease the bolt forward with the release, then push the two trigger group pins through the receiver with a punch. Either side works on the SX4 — unlike some guns these pins are not directional — so pick the side that lets you support the receiver, and pull them out from the far side once they stand proud. Then take hold of the trigger guard and lift the whole group up and out of the receiver. Keep the punch square so it does not skid across and scratch the alloy receiver.
steps.prose: The trigger group carries hammer, sear, trigger and carrier release as a unit. It comes out as one piece and goes back as one piece.
steps.quote: Use a punch or similar object to push inward on the trigger group pins, taking care not to scratch the receiver. Trigger group pins may be removed from either side of the receiver. Push the trigger group pins through the receiver. Pull on them from the opposite side to remove them (Figure 18).
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REMOVING THE TRIGGER GROUP, step 2

steps.title: The trigger group does not come apart
steps.action: Clean the trigger group as an assembly and do not take it any further. Winchester's notice is flat and carries no exception — everything inside it is a small sprung part fitted in relation to the others, and there is no published order to put them back in. The published cleaning method matches that: flush it with a quality aerosol gun solvent, let it dry, and then very lightly oil the moving parts. That reaches everything without a single part coming off.
steps.prose: Aerosol is doing real work here. It drives solvent into pivots you cannot see and carries the grime back out with it.
steps.quote: NOTICE: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE TRIGGER GROUP BEYOND THIS POINT.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REMOVING THE TRIGGER GROUP, step 4 NOTICE
steps.warn: The trigger group is cleaned assembled. It is never opened.

steps.title: Bolt handle out — and 12 and 20 gauge do it differently
steps.action: With the trigger group out, the barrel and gas parts off, and the bolt eased forward under control, pull the bolt handle out of the bolt. On a 12 gauge that is all there is to it: it draws straight outward. On a 20 gauge it is retained, and you must hold the shotgun with the loading port UP and press the shell stop while pulling the handle outward. Pulling harder on a 20 gauge handle without touching the shell stop will not free it and risks bending the handle.
steps.prose: Note which gauge you have now, because reassembly forks the same way and the 20 gauge has an extra catch to feel for.
steps.caution: 20 gauge: loading port up, press the shell stop, THEN pull the handle.
steps.quote: On 12 gauge models, remove the bolt handle by pulling it outward (Figure 20).
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REMOVING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY, step 5

steps.title: Bolt assembly forward and out of the receiver
steps.action: With the handle out, slide the bolt assembly forward and out of the front of the receiver — on a 20 gauge you again press the shell stop and take the bolt and bolt slide out together. Once it is on the bench the bolt and the bolt slide can be separated from each other for cleaning, which exposes the bolt slide rails and the link that drives the whole system. That separation is the last thing this manual publishes for the bolt.
steps.prose: The receiver cavity is now open from both ends, which is the real point of going this deep.
steps.quote: The bolt and bolt slide can be separated for cleaning (Figure 23). Perform any cleaning of the bolt and receiver cavity as necessary.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REMOVING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY, step 7

steps.title: The bolt assembly stops at the bolt and the bolt slide
steps.action: Do not take the bolt itself apart. Winchester's notice ends the procedure at the bolt-and-bolt-slide split, which means the locking head, the firing pin and its retaining pin, the extractor and their springs all stay where they are. Those parts sit inside a rotating bolt head under spring load and there is no published reassembly for them. Clean what is now exposed and stop.
steps.prose: The manual also says plainly that no further disassembly is required for cleaning. Take that at face value.
steps.quote: NOTICE: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY BEYOND THIS POINT.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REMOVING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY, step 7 NOTICE
steps.warn: Bolt and bolt slide separate. Nothing inside the bolt comes out.

steps.title: Nothing else on this shotgun is an owner's part
steps.action: The manual closes with the same limit stated as a general rule: never take the firearm apart further than the book explains, because the inner mechanism can be permanently damaged by the attempt. On an SX4 that covers the carrier and its spring, the shell stops, the recoil spring and follower in the stock, and everything inside the two assemblies you have just cleaned. When something genuinely needs to come out, it goes to a qualified gunsmith or to the Arnold, Missouri facility.
steps.prose: After extended heavy use, Winchester's own recommendation is exactly that — a gunsmith stripping the action for professional cleaning and lubrication.
steps.quote: NOTICE: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL. YOUR FIREARM IS A SPECIALIZED, FINELY FITTED MECHANISM. YOU MAY PERMANENTLY DAMAGE IT BY ATTEMPTING TO DISASSEMBLE THE INNER MECHANISM.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — closing NOTICE

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should be looking at the barrel, the forearm, the magazine cap, the gas piston, the piston sleeve and its spring, the trigger group with its two pins, the bolt handle, the bolt and bolt slide, and the receiver with the stock. That is the complete published Super X4 strip. Keep the gas parts as a set — they go back on the magazine tube in a specific order with the push rod on a specific side of the receiver by gauge. Deep Clean covers the bore from the breech, the gas system's nylon-brush-only routine, the receiver cavity, and the reassembly sequence that has to be followed exactly.
steps.prose: Remember the standing rule while it is apart: nothing gets released forward onto an empty receiver mouth.
steps.quote: The trigger group and bolt assembly of your Super X®4 shotgun are designed to be removed in the field, without special tools.
steps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies

deepSteps.title: Bore from the BREECH end, and the choke threads with it
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off, run a lightly oiled patch on a shotgun rod into the BREECH end and back and forth several times — barrel off means the crown never has to take a rod, so use that. While the barrel is in your hands, take the choke tube out and wipe the tube, its threads and the barrel threads with a nylon brush and a light oil. Those threads are where fouling turns a removable choke into a seized one, and they are only reachable at this moment.
deepSteps.prose: Do the thread work at every cleaning, not occasionally. Winchester asks for it after each use and before a tube goes back in.
deepSteps.quote: Using a shotgun cleaning rod with a slotted tip or cleaning jag and a patch large enough for a snug fit in the bore, insert the rod and a lightly oiled patch in the breech end of the barrel and run back and forth through the bore several times. Remove and wipe the choke tube, choke tube threads, and barrel threads with a nylon brush and lightly oil.
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — CLEANING THE BARREL, step 3

deepSteps.title: Never run a brass brush through a choke-tubed barrel with no tube in it
deepSteps.action: If the bore needs a brass brush, put a choke tube in FIRST. With the tube out, the threads at the muzzle are exposed and bristles that break off lodge in them, after which fitting and removing tubes becomes a fight. The same rule covers firing: never fire the shotgun, and never run cleaning tools through it, without a choke tube installed — the exposed threads are the thing being protected in both cases.
deepSteps.prose: Powder solvent first, brush pushed fully through before pulling back, exactly as on any bore. It is where the brush is allowed to go that is specific to a choke-tubed gun.
deepSteps.quote: Never use a brass brush to clean your barrels unless choke tubes are installed. Bristles could break off and lodge in the threads, making installation and removal of the choke tubes difficult.
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — CLEANING THE INVECTOR - PLUS CHOKE SYSTEM, step 1
deepSteps.warn: Choke tube in before any brass brush, and before firing.

deepSteps.title: Leading and plastic — look from both ends before you decide
deepSteps.action: Inspect the bore from the breech and from the muzzle. What you are looking for is longitudinal streaking of lead and of plastic from the shot cups, concentrated near the muzzle and just forward of the chamber. Some of both is normal on a shotgun and needs no action. Looking from one end only conceals one of the two problem zones, which is why the manual specifies both.
deepSteps.prose: Excessive plastic is what starts to move the pattern, and it builds slowly enough that you only see it if you look each time.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the bore from both ends for leading and plastic residue that often remains in the bores from the shot cups in modern shells. Leading and plastic residue will appear as longitudinal streaks and are usually more predominant near the muzzle and just forward of the chamber.
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — CLEANING THE BARREL, step 4

deepSteps.title: Gas system — nylon brush only, and never a steel one
deepSteps.action: Spray the magazine tube, the gas piston and the piston sleeve with gun solvent and work them over thoroughly with a NYLON brush. For heavy carbon on the tube and inside the piston, Winchester nominates a green kitchen scrub pad. Two things are forbidden and both matter: never a steel brush on any gas system component, because these are close-tolerance sliding surfaces and scoring them changes how the piston seals; and do not remove the spring inside the piston. Taking the piston sleeve spring off does make the inside of the sleeve easier to reach, and that one is allowed.
deepSteps.prose: Finish with a light film of oil on every gas part for protection and lubrication. The gas system needs only occasional cleaning, but it needs it done properly.
deepSteps.quote: Do not remove the spring inside of the piston. Never use a steel brush on any of the gas system components.
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — CLEANING THE GAS SYSTEM, step 2
deepSteps.warn: Nylon brush only. No steel brush anywhere on the gas system.

deepSteps.title: Receiver cavity — clean, oil, then wipe it dry
deepSteps.action: With the trigger group and bolt out, use a gun solvent and a nylon brush to loosen caked grime in the receiver, wipe the cavity clean, then oil it lightly and wipe it back off. That last move is deliberate: what you want left behind is a protective film, not a reservoir, because a gas gun's receiver collects unburnt powder and an oily receiver turns that into paste. The manual states outright that no further disassembly is required to clean it.
deepSteps.prose: This is the step to do after a wet day or a dusty one. It is also the fix Winchester suggests trying before sending a malfunctioning gun anywhere.
deepSteps.quote: Wipe the receiver cavity clean. Lightly oil the cavity and wipe it dry. No further disassembly is required for cleaning.
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — CLEANING THE ACTION, step 1

deepSteps.title: Trigger group: aerosol solvent, dry, then a very light oil
deepSteps.action: Clean the trigger group as an assembly with a quality aerosol gun solvent, let it dry fully, and then very lightly oil only the moving parts. Letting it dry before oiling is the part people skip — oil sprayed onto wet solvent is diluted and runs off, and what is left in the sear engagement afterwards is neither one thing nor the other. Hold the group so the solvent runs OUT rather than pooling in the trigger guard.
deepSteps.prose: Work the trigger and hammer by hand a few times while it is out to see the parts move and confirm nothing is gritty.
deepSteps.quote: We suggest cleaning the trigger group with a quality aerosol gun solvent. Allow it to dry and then very lightly oil the moving parts.
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REMOVING THE TRIGGER GROUP, step 4

deepSteps.title: Bolt back in: oil the grooves, then find the link's socket
deepSteps.action: Reassemble the bolt to the bolt slide, put a few drops of oil in the receiver grooves that the bolt slide rails run in, and slide the assembly back in LINK END FIRST with the rails aligned to the grooves. Then guide the bolt slide link into its socket in the recoil spring follower — that is the connection between the bolt and the spring in the stock, and if it is not engaged the gun will feel assembled and will not cycle. Open and close the action several times afterwards to prove the link and the follower are properly engaged.
deepSteps.prose: On a 20 gauge, refitting the bolt handle needs the loading port up and the shell stop pressed, and you may have to pull the handle out slightly until the shell stop clicks back — miss that and the magazine will not load.
deepSteps.quote: Align the rails on the bolt slide with the grooves in the sides of the receiver and place the bolt assembly back in the receiver, bolt slide link end first (Figure 25).
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Trigger Group and Bolt Assemblies — REINSTALLING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY, step 2

deepSteps.title: Two drops in the right places beats a bottle in the receiver
deepSteps.action: Put oil where the manual points it: a drop of lightweight gun oil on the receiver rails the bolt slides on, and a drop on the surface of the magazine tube where the gas piston rides. Those are the two friction paths that decide whether an SX4 cycles smoothly. Then stop — excess oil runs back into the wood of the stock and softens it, which loosens the stock on the receiver permanently. If the gun has been in dust, mud or water, wipe the principal working parts INCLUDING the gas system clean and re-lubricate lightly.
deepSteps.prose: The same restraint applies in cold weather, where surplus oil thickens and slows a gas gun's cycle directly.
deepSteps.quote: NOTICE: DO NOT PLACE LARGE QUANTITIES OF OIL INTO THE ACTION. EXCESS OIL WILL RUN BACK INTO THE WOOD OF THE STOCK SOFTENING THE WOOD, WITH CONSEQUENTIAL LOOSENING OF THE STOCK.
deepSteps.cite: SX4 Owner's Manuals — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — PERIODIC OILING NOTICE
deepSteps.warn: Never pour oil into the action.

cleaning.name: BARREL, BORE & CHOKE
tasks: Barrel off the gun, then a lightly oiled patch from the BREECH end
Choke tube out; wipe the tube, its threads and the barrel threads with a nylon brush and light oil
Threads cleaned after each use and before a tube goes back in
Inspect the bore from BOTH ends for lead and plastic streaking
Brass brush only with a choke tube installed, solvent first, pushed fully through before pulling back
Dry patch, then one lightly oiled patch; confirm no patch is left in barrel or chamber
Never fire or run cleaning tools through the barrel without a choke tube installed

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM (Active Valve)
tasks: Gas piston, piston sleeve and piston sleeve spring off the magazine tube
Solvent plus a NYLON brush on the magazine tube, piston and sleeve — never a steel brush
A green kitchen scrub pad for heavy carbon on the tube and inside the piston
The piston sleeve spring may come out to reach the sleeve interior; the spring INSIDE the piston must not
Light film of oil on every gas part afterwards
A drop of oil on the magazine tube surface where the piston slides

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, BOLT & TRIGGER GROUP
tasks: Trigger group out first, then the bolt — never the other way round
Solvent and a nylon brush on caked grime; wipe the receiver cavity, oil it lightly, wipe it dry
Trigger group cleaned as an assembly with aerosol solvent, dried, then very lightly oiled — never opened
Bolt and bolt slide separated for cleaning; nothing inside the bolt comes out
A few drops of oil in the receiver grooves the bolt slide rails run in
Never let the bolt run forward under spring power with the barrel off

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STOCK
tasks: Wipe all exposed metal with an oiled cloth and remove every finger mark
Re-oil after exposure to weather or handling
Wood: a lightweight gun oil OR a quality furniture wax — not both
Keep DEET insect repellent and sunscreen off the finishes
Never pour oil into the action; it soaks into the stock and loosens it

reassembly: Reassemble the bolt and bolt slide, oil the receiver grooves, and insert the bolt assembly link end first with the rails aligned to the grooves.
Guide the bolt slide link into its socket in the recoil spring follower.

Refit the bolt handle: 12 gauge, straight into its slot in the bolt. 20 gauge, loading port up, press the shell stop while inserting it, then pull out slightly until the shell stop clicks back — or the magazine will not load.
Open and close the action several times to confirm the bolt slide link and recoil spring follower are properly engaged, holding the handle so the bolt never slams onto an empty receiver.
With the bolt forward, fit the trigger group into the receiver, align its holes with the receiver holes, and tap the two pins home with a plastic or wooden mallet.

Lock the bolt rearward, then slide the piston sleeve spring and piston sleeve onto the magazine tube push-rod end first — push rod into the LEFT-side receiver slot on 12 gauge models, the RIGHT-side slot on 20 gauge.

Slide the gas piston into the gas bracket, align both over the magazine tube and slide them on so the barrel extension drops solidly into the receiver, and confirm the push rod moves freely in its slot.
Slide the forearm onto the magazine tube and over the gas bracket until it seats, and fit the magazine cap finger tight.
Open and close the action several times, then retighten the magazine cap to ensure a proper seal.
Confirm the safety is on safe and wipe the exterior down.
fncheck: With the shotgun unloaded, look through the bore from both ends against a light and confirm it is clear and that no patch remains, with the correct choke tube fitted and firmly seated. Confirm the magazine cap is finger tight after the action has been cycled a few times — a cap that loosens as the gun settles is what makes a gas gun short-stroke. Cycle the bolt handle several times and confirm it locks rearward on an empty magazine and runs home cleanly with the barrel installed. Check the push rod moves freely in its slot in the receiver. On a 20 gauge, load and remove a dummy shell to confirm the shell stop clicked back after the bolt handle was refitted. Work the safety both ways and confirm the trigger cannot be pulled on safe, remembering which hand your gun is set up for. Leave the safety on safe.
